title: Libraries are expanding their civic role while aging facilities constrain access and resilience
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107262 nationally representative survey and site study of public library facilities
geography: United States; public libraries in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and four territories, including tribal libraries in site visits

poor_building_system.unit: estimated percent of public libraries with at least one building system, such as HVAC, in poor condition

health_safety_concern.unit: estimated percent with at least one building system or feature posing a potential health or safety concern

observations.method: GAO nationally representative survey of approximately 16,400 public libraries, supplemented by visits to 21 public and two tribal libraries in seven states and territories.
observations.uncertainty: Facility conditions are reported or estimated at the library level and do not measure actual service interruption, building-by-building engineering risk, or user outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Public libraries, small and rural libraries, tribal libraries, libraries serving high-poverty areas, people with disabilities, and communities relying on library facilities.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported poor system or potential concern does not mean a building is unusable; libraries may maintain service through repairs, relocation, partnerships, or partial access.

observations.period: 2025 survey; deferred maintenance and repair backlog

deferred_maintenance.unit: estimated percent of public libraries with a deferred-maintenance and repair backlog

backlog_persistence.unit: estimated percent expecting deferred maintenance to persist or increase over the next three years

large_backlog.unit: estimated percent with a deferred-maintenance backlog exceeding $100,000

observations.method: GAO survey estimates and review of budget forecasts, planned projects, and reported repair-cost examples.
observations.uncertainty: The total national repair cost is unknown; backlog thresholds and expectations are reported estimates, not audited capital-needs assessments or forecasts of actual failure.
observations.subgroup: Libraries with aging facilities, high repair needs, small-town and rural libraries, and libraries with limited capital access.
observations.counterinterpretation: A backlog can be reduced through local capital campaigns, grants, phased projects, or partnerships even when libraries currently expect persistence; planned persistence is not inevitable failure.

physical_access_barrier.unit: approximately public libraries reporting a physical barrier to access for people with disabilities

construction_funding_challenge.unit: estimated percent citing construction costs and limited funding as key repair challenges

local_funding_repair.unit: estimated percent using local funding to address maintenance and repairs

civic_functions.value: libraries provide public space for community programs and can serve as voting sites and emergency centers in addition to lending materials

observations.method: GAO survey, site visits, and interviews with federal, state, tribal, library, and stakeholder officials.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not estimate how many users are excluded by each barrier, whether alternative sites exist, or how local funding decisions affect other public services.
observations.subgroup: People with disabilities, voters, emergency users, community-program participants, library staff, and communities with small or high-poverty tax bases.
observations.counterinterpretation: Local funding can reflect community commitment and preserve autonomy; the concern is that reliance on limited local bases may make access uneven, not that local funding is inherently inadequate.

service_expectation.value: libraries are expected to provide programming, technology access, community space, emergency support, and voting infrastructure in addition to books

funding_mismatch.value: federal support generally covers programs and services but not construction or repairs

capacity_risk.value: aging facilities can constrain libraries' ability to meet expanded community-service expectations

observations.method: GAO synthesis of facility conditions, funding rules, community functions, and stakeholder evidence.
observations.uncertainty: The study does not establish that facility condition caused lower civic participation, worse emergency response, reduced digital access, or declining institutional trust.
observations.subgroup: Library users, nonusers who rely on public facilities during emergencies, voters, students, job seekers, immigrants, older adults, and local governments.
observations.counterinterpretation: Programs, partnerships, mobile services, and digital delivery can partly substitute for buildings; physical public space remains a distinct capacity rather than the only route to service.

related_sources.claim: GAO's full report and accessible materials provide the detailed survey, site-visit, and methodology documentation.

boundary: This record adds a civic-infrastructure route linking public-library facility condition, maintenance finance, accessibility, technology and emergency functions, and community capacity. It does not establish user-level exclusion, service interruption, causal civic effects, or the total national capital requirement.
